bibl.note: Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek; shelfmark Res/4 Astr.p. 90 h#Beibd.18. Leaves: A1v. Leaf designations inherited from the image collection; some are inferred.
The dedication prints M. D: XXXV. This reading is retained, not silently changed to 1534. Both retrieved copies show the same date and apparent setting; no separate edition is asserted.

editorialDecl.p: Complete English translation; spelling and names follow readable English conventions. Your Worships renders the variable civic honorifics approximately; mayors renders Stetmeister without implying identity with a modern mayoralty. Predictive Astronomia/Astronomei is generally translated astrology, with the historical overlap of astronomy and astrology acknowledged. Historical assertions and attributed authorities are translated as presented, without endorsing or authenticating them.

Editorial English paragraph divisions and punctuation do not reproduce printed lineation. Each translationSegment div has @corresp linking the first and last German xml:id in an inclusive source-line range; a single link denotes one line. The ranges cover all transcribed lines exactly once. Brackets mark explanatory supplies or tentative readings; the end notes discuss uncertainties. Source images and their provenance remain linked in the German TEI. No missing preface is reconstructed.

div.head: Anton Brelochs: English translation of the dedicatory preface for 1535

div.p: To the steadfast, honorable, prudent, respected, and wise mayors and council of the city of Schwäbisch Hall, my gracious and dear lords in authority.

Steadfast, honorable, prudent, and wise lords: I first offer Your Worships my most willing and diligent service. Gracious and dear lords in authority, in order to maintain my longstanding custom, I have again undertaken to describe the future events of this present year, fifteen hundred and thirty-five. Accordingly, I have drawn them from the teaching of those learned in the stars and have once again set them down in a practica, which I present to Your Worships in the customary manner. I humbly ask that you graciously accept it from me, interpret it in the most favorable light, and continue to regard me as commended to your care as your humble and willing servant. Dated on the Sunday after St. Pantaleon’s Day, the second of August, in the year 1535 [as printed].
Your Worships’ obedient servant, Dr. Antonius Brelochs.

div.head: Translation notes
div.note: The dedication prints M. D: XXXV. (1535), as does the alternate Augsburg witness. This potentially problematic date is retained; no correction to 1534 is imposed.
Gebietenden identifies the civic authorities as those who govern or command; it is rendered with “lords in authority.”
The feast reference and numbered day are retained without attempting to reconcile them.
